Our flights

Our business class flights

The idea is simple: cross the Atlantic in business class, in seats that fold down into a real bed, so we arrive rested instead of exhausted. Once we land in Europe, a short connecting flight — economy is perfectly fine for an hour or three — takes us the rest of the way. The flights below are real and available right now, checked on October 22, 2026. Nothing is booked yet: Alex will confirm everything before anything is reserved, and the flights would be booked with Alex’s points.

Where the flights are pointing: right now, the availability lines up most clearly for Andalusia, in southern Spain. Malta is the other strong option — and it uses some of the very same flights.

Andalusia · Option 1

Through Madrid

New York (JFK) → Madrid, non-stop in business class with American Airlines — lie-flat seats for the overnight flight.

Depart Monday, November 16 · Return Wednesday, November 25 (Tuesday the 24th or Thursday the 26th also work) · About 10 days

From Madrid, it is just a 1-hour flight down to Málaga — or a high-speed train straight to Seville.

Andalusia · Option 2

Through Zurich

Montreal → Zurich, non-stop in business class with Swiss — lie-flat seats for the overnight flight.

Depart Monday, November 16 · Return Friday, November 27 · About 11 days

Then Zurich → Málaga is a non-stop flight of about 2 hours 45. And this option departs from Montreal — close to home for Mom.

Andalusia · Option 3

Through Frankfurt

Atlanta → Frankfurt in business class with Lufthansa — lie-flat seats for the overnight flight.

Depart Tuesday, November 17 · Return Wednesday, November 25 or Thursday, November 26 (landing in Miami) · About 9 to 10 days

From Frankfurt, Málaga is a non-stop flight of about 3 hours.

The other option

Malta, with the same flights

If we choose Malta instead, we can take the same Zurich or Frankfurt flights above — from there, it is a short flight of about 2½ to 3 hours down to Malta, on the same dates.

Only the last little hop changes — everything else stays the same.

A little note of reassurance: award seats like these come and go, so availability may shift a little. Alex is keeping an eye on it and will lock in the flights as soon as we have chosen our destination together. And every option above has us home before December 1.
